Method of Attack: PowerShell-based ransomware encrypting devices without additional components
Steals saved user credentials from email clients (Mozilla Thunderbird, Microsoft Outlook) and web browsers (Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome)
Harvests credentials by accessing registry keys or application folders
Delivers stolen credentials to command-and-control server via Base64 encoded POST requests
Arrives via spam emails with malicious Word documents dropping JasperLoader downloader
Gains persistence by adding scheduled task and shortcut to Startup folder
Checks for killswitch file before encryption
Disables Windows recovery environment and deletes Shadow Volume Copies and backups
Encrypts files adding .FTCODE extension and ransom notes
Impacted Systems: Windows devices running at least Windows 7 or Windows Server 2008 R2
Email clients: Mozilla Thunderbird, Microsoft Outlook
Web browsers: Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome
Attack Vector: Spam emails containing malicious Word documents disguised as invoices, scans, resumes
Indicators of Compromise: POST requests to command-and-control (C2) server with Base64 encoded credentials
